title: System context
question: Who uses the system and what connects to it?
rule: Show one focal system and label interactions with people and external systems.

title: Use case
question: What can each role do?
rule: Group goals inside the system. Keep actor associations undirected and label include or extend dependencies.

title: Functional decomposition
question: How is the work broken down?
rule: Use verb phrases and parent-child decomposition. Link ownership and requirements by reference.

title: Capability map
question: What can the organisation do?
rule: Nest business capabilities. Keep ownership and maturity in the details.

title: Container
question: What runs independently?
rule: Group runtime units under the system. Show technology and protocol; keep code-level components out.

title: Component
question: What lives inside a runtime unit?
rule: Group modules inside their container. Point dependencies from caller to dependency and name ports where known.

title: Layers
question: Which layers can depend on each other?
rule: Order layer bands. Show actual dependency direction and flag edges that violate an explicit layer policy.

title: Package dependencies
question: Which packages depend on each other?
rule: Use qualified names, import or manifest evidence, and report dependency cycles.

title: Class
question: What types and methods make up the code?
rule: Use separate field and method compartments. Show inheritance, composition and endpoint multiplicities.

title: Domain model
question: How do business concepts relate?
rule: Use business vocabulary, named associations, cardinalities and linked business rules.

title: Sequence
question: Who sends what, in what order?
rule: Order messages explicitly. Include return messages and use labelled fragments for alternatives, loops and concurrency.

title: Event flow
question: Where do events go after publication?
rule: Show versioned event names through topics to consumers and attach subscription filters and delivery policies.

title: Activity / workflow
question: How does work move through decisions?
rule: Place actions in owner lanes, with explicit start, end, branch guards, and fork/join when applicable.

title: State machine
question: What changes state, and what allows it?
rule: Show initial and final markers and cycles. Label transitions with the event, guard and action.

title: User journey
question: What does someone experience from start to finish?
rule: Order stage cards and attach touchpoints, goals and observed pain points to stable stage IDs.

title: Data flow
question: Where does data enter, move and persist?
rule: Label flows with data payloads and route data-store flows through a process.

title: Entity relationships
question: How do database tables link?
rule: Show typed columns, keys and nullability. Attach foreign keys to named columns and show cardinality.

title: Data lineage
question: Which source fields produce each result?
rule: Name datasets, transformation steps and field mappings. Trace result fields back to their origins.

title: Integration
question: What crosses a system boundary?
rule: Identify transfer direction, contract, transport and version for each integration.

title: API interaction
question: How does a request reach an operation?
rule: Show caller, gateway route and operation. Compare method and path and expose request and response schemas.

title: Deployment
question: Where does each runtime unit execute?
rule: Group execution nodes by environment. Show artifact placement and distinguish replicas by count.

title: Network topology
question: Which network paths carry traffic?
rule: Group endpoints by network segment. Label directed traffic with protocol and destination port.

title: Trust boundaries
question: Where does data cross a trust boundary?
rule: Group nodes by trust zone and attach data classification and named security controls to crossings.

title: Authentication & authorisation
question: How are requests allowed or denied?
rule: Separate sign-in, token validation and authorization and show distinct denial outcomes.

title: Observability
question: How do we detect and investigate problems?
rule: Route logs, metrics and traces distinctly. Bind alert conditions, evaluation windows and owners to the metric source.

title: Failover & recovery
question: How is service restored after a failure?
rule: Show detection, failover, verification and escalation. Reference recovery objectives and runbooks.

title: CI/CD pipeline
question: What has to pass before release?
rule: Model job prerequisites, parallel checks, approval gates and artifact identity. Reject prerequisite cycles.

title: Migration & transition
question: How does the solution change safely?
rule: Order phases, reuse shared IDs and record changes, cutover checks and rollback targets.
